claim: The chick retina consists of three cellular layers: outer nuclear layer (ONL), inner nuclear layer (INL), and ganglion cell layer (GCL) separated by two synaptic layers, outer plexiform (OPL) and inner plexiform (IPL).
source: The retina consists of three cellular layers: outer nuclear layer (ONL), inner nuclear layer (INL), and ganglion cell layer (GCL) separated by two synaptic layers, outer plexiform (OPL) and inner plexiform (IPL).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in Figure 1A caption and the visual evidence in Figure 1A showing the retinal structure.

claim: The ONL contains photoreceptors including double cones, single cones, and rods.
source: The ONL contains photoreceptors (PR): double cones, single cones, and rods.
evidence: The claim is stated in the Figure 1B caption and illustrated in the sketch.

claim: The INL contains horizontal, bipolar, and amacrine cells (HC, BC, and AC) and Müller glia (MG).
source: The INL contains horizontal, bipolar, and amacrine cells (HC, BC, and AC) and Müller glia (MG).
evidence: The claim is stated in the Figure 1B caption and illustrated in the sketch.

claim: The GCL contains retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and ACs.
source: The GCL contains retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and ACs.
evidence: The claim is stated in the Figure 1B caption and illustrated in the sketch.

claim: Oligodendrocytes (OL) are present in an axonal layer beneath the GCL.
source: Oligodendrocytes (OL) are present in an axonal layer beneath the GCL.
evidence: The claim is stated in the Figure 1B caption and illustrated in the sketch.

claim: Hatching (P0) occurs at embryonic day (E)21 in chicks.
source: Hatching (P0) is at embryonic day (E)21.
evidence: The claim is stated in the Figure 1C caption.

claim: 30,022 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from embryonic day 18 (E18) chick retina.
source: We used a droplet-based method (Zheng et al., 2017) to obtain 30,022 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes from embryonic day 18 (E18) chick retina (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section describing the profiling of chick retinal cells.

claim: Five neuronal classes (PRs, HCs, BCs, ACs, and RGCs) and two glial types (Müller glia and oligodendrocytes) were identified from E18 retinal cells.
source: We identified five neuronal classes (PRs, HCs, BCs, ACs, and RGCs) as well as two glial types, Müller glia and oligodendrocytes (Figure 1D,E,F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1D, E, F.

claim: Of the E18 retinal cells profiled, 620 were RGCs, representing approximately 2% of the total.
source: Of the E18 retinal cells profiled, 620 were RGCs (Figure 1F). This fraction (~2%) was similar to that observed in other species (Macosko et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2019) but was insufficient for extensive classification of what we anticipated would be a highly heterogeneous class.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by citation to other species.

claim: Magnetic beads coated with antibodies to the pan-RGC cell surface marker Thy1 were used to enrich RGCs from E16 retina before scRNA-seq.
source: We therefore used magnetic beads coated with antibodies to the pan-RGC cell surface marker Thy1 (French and Jeffrey, 1986; Yamagata et al., 2002) to enrich RGCs from E16 retina before scRNA-seq.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: 9159 single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from E16 retina, of which 8107 (89%) were RGCs.
source: We obtained 9159 single-cell transcriptomes, of which 8107 (89%) were RGCs (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) that were used for subsequent analysis.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1G.

claim: A total of 150 clusters were obtained by reclustering each cell class separately.
source: To resolve cell types within these classes, we reclustered each one separately, and obtained a total of 150 clusters (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1H.

claim: Each cluster presumably corresponded to a cell type, a small group of closely related types, a positional variant or a developmental intermediate.
source: Each presumably corresponded to a cell type, a small group of closely related types, a positional variant or, since we profiled embryonic cells, a developmental intermediate.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the clustering results.

claim: eCHIKIN (electroporation- and CRISPR-mediated Homology-Instructed Knock-IN) was developed to insert fluorescent reporters into genes expressed by specific cell types.
source: We call the method eCHIKIN for electroporation- and CRISPR-mediated Homology-Instructed Knock-IN.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section describing the method development.

claim: eCHIKIN uses in ovo electroporation to deliver a mixture consisting of guide RNAs, Cas9 protein, and a single-strand DNA containing a reporter sequence flanked by ~70 bases gene-specific homology arms.
source: We used in ovo electroporation to deliver a mixture consisting of guide RNAs, Cas9 protein, and a single-strand DNA containing a reporter sequence flanked by ~70 bases gene-specific homology arms (Gurumurthy et al., 2019; Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: VSX2-HA-tagged cells were restricted to the outer part of the INL, as appropriate for BCs, and were VSX2-positive and TFAP2A-negative.
source: VSX2-HA-tagged cells were restricted in the outer part of the INL, as appropriate for BCs, and were VSX2-positive and TFAP2A-negative (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B-D showing immunostaining results.

claim: TFAP2A-GFP cells were present in the inner portion of the INL as appropriate for TFAP2A-expressing ACs.
source: TFAP2A-GFP cells were present in the inner portion of the INL as appropriate for TFAP2A-expressing ACs (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: RBPMS2-HA-tagged cells were confined to the ganglion cell layer, as appropriate for RGCs.
source: Likewise, RBPMS2-HA-tagged cells were confined to the ganglion cell layer, as appropriate for RGCs (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2F.

claim: Chicks are tetrachromatic, with cone types that express red opsin (OPN1LW), green opsin (OPN1MSW), blue opsin (OPN2SW), or violet opsin (OPN1SW).
source: Chicks are tetrachromatic, with cone types that express red opsin (OPN1LW), green opsin (OPN1MSW), blue opsin (OPN2SW), or violet opsin (OPN1SW) (Kram et al., 2010; Enright et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Chick retina contains rods that express rhodopsin (RHO) and OPN1LW-expressing 'double-cones' (DCs) composed of tightly apposed principal and accessory cells.
source: In addition to these conventional 'single-cones' (SCs), the retina also contains rods that express rhodopsin (RHO) and OPN1LW-expressing 'double-cones' (DCs) composed of tightly apposed principal and accessory cells, which together comprise about half of all PRs (Smith et al., 1985; López-López et al., 2008; Oishi et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Reclustering of PRs revealed 12 clusters, including one each expressing RHO, OPN1MSW, OPN2SW, and OPN1SW, marking them as rods and green, blue, and violet SCs, respectively.
source: Reclustering of PRs revealed 12 clusters (numbered in order of descending abundance; Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), including one each expressing RHO, OPN1MSW, OPN2SW, and OPN1SW (PR clusters 3, 5, 8, and 11), marking them as rods and green, blue, and violet SCs, respectively (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Expression of OPN1LW was detected in four clusters (PR clusters 1, 2, 4, and 7), representing red SCs and DCs.
source: Expression of OPN1LW was detected in four clusters (PR clusters 1, 2, 4, and 7; Figure 3B), representing red SCs and DCs.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: PR7 is identified as red SCs and PR1, 2, and 4 as components of DCs.
source: Thus, we identify PR7 as red SCs and PR1, 2, and 4 as components of DCs.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Four PR clusters expressed the PR fate determination gene PRDM1 but did not express opsins, suggesting that they were immature PRs.
source: The third clade of PRs, comprising four clusters, expressed the PR fate determination gene, PRDM1 (Katoh et al., 2010; Brzezinski et al., 2013), but did not express opsins, suggesting that they were immature PRs.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: At E12, ARHGAP18 was expressed by PRs in the ONL, but OPN1LW was not detectable.
source: At E12, ARHGAP18 was expressed by PRs in the ONL, but OPN1LW was not detectable.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section describing in situ hybridization results.

claim: At E20, OPN1LW was expressed but ARGHAP18 was not.
source: Conversely, OPN1LW was expressed at E20 but ARGHAP18 was not (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D), suggesting that ARGHAP18 is transiently expressed in the ONL during development.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: At E16, ARHGAP18 and SLIT1 were expressed by ONL cells selectively in peripheral retina, whereas OPN1LW and STRA6 were expressed by ONL cells in central retina.
source: At E16, consistent with the fact that retinal differentiation proceeds in a central-to-peripheral gradient (Kahn, 1974; Spence and Robson, 1989; Prada et al., 1991; Bruhn and Cepko, 1996), ARHGAP18 and SLIT1 were expressed by ONL cells selectively in peripheral retina, whereas OPN1LW and STRA6 were by ONL cells in central retina (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–Q).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–Q.

claim: Clustering of E18 HCs yielded five clusters, HC1-5, all expressing the canonical HC marker ONECUT3.
source: Clustering of E18 HCs yielded five clusters, HC1-5 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), all expressing the canonical HC marker ONECUT3.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: LHX1 and ISL1 were detected in exclusive HC populations.
source: LHX1 and ISL1 were detected in exclusive populations and other markers distinguished each type (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: HC1 and HC3 correspond to Type I HCs and HC2/HC4/HC5 to Type II HCs.
source: Based on prior immunohistochemical analysis (Fischer et al., 2007; Edqvist et al., 2008), we hypothesized that HC1 and HC3 corresponded to Type I and HC2/HC4/HC5 to Type II HCs.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: HC1 is a mature type and HC3 its immature counterpart.
source: Thus, we conclude that HC1 is a mature type and HC3 its immature counterpart.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section as a conclusion from spatiotemporal analysis.

claim: HC2, HC4, and HC5 were distinguished by selective and non-overlapping expression of distinct receptor-type tyrosine kinases, NTRK1, EGFR, and LTK, respectively.
source: The ISL1+LHX1- types HC2, HC4, and HC5 were distinguished by selective and non-overlapping expression of distinct receptor-type tyrosine kinases, NTRK1, EGFR, and LTK, respectively (Figure 4B,D–I).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4B, D-I.

claim: Unsupervised clustering identified 22 groups of BCs ranging in frequency from 1.5 to 10.4% of all BCs.
source: Unsupervised clustering of our data identified 22 groups of BCs (Figure 5A) ranging in frequency from 1.5 to 10.4% of all BCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All BC clusters expressed the canonical markers VSX2 and OTX2, and each was distinguished by selective expression of other genes.
source: All expressed the canonical markers VSX2 and OTX2, and each was distinguished by selective expression of other genes (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: The expression of GRIK1 was mutually exclusive with that of TRPM1 and ISL1 in all BC clusters but one, resulting in 11 likely ON types and 10 likely OFF types.
source: In our dataset, the expression of GRIK1 was mutually exclusive with that of TRPM1 and ISL1 in all clusters but one, resulting in 11 likely ON types and 10 likely OFF types (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: PRKCA was expressed at highest levels in BC19, a putative ON cluster, suggesting that it might represent rod BCs.
source: PRKCA was expressed at highest levels in BC19, a putative ON cluster, suggesting that it might represent rod BCs (Greferath et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: BC10, which expresses both ON and OFF markers, might have mixed properties.
source: BC10, which expresses both ON and OFF markers might have mixed properties, as has been seen in fish (Yn et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: BC1 axons terminated in S3, BC6 and BC8 axons in S3, and BC15 in S4; BC12 axons were bistratified with termini in S1 and S2.
source: As shown in Figure 5D–H, BC1 axons terminated in S3, BC6 and BC8 axons in S3, and BC15 in S4; BC12 axons were bistratified with termini in S1 and S2.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D-H showing eCHIKIN labeling.

claim: Somata of putative OFF (GRIK1+) and ON (TRPM1+) BCs were situated in the outer and inner portions of the INL, respectively, corresponding to the positions of their axon terminals.
source: Somata of putative OFF (GRIK1+) and ON (TRPM1+) BCs were situated in the outer and inner portions of the INL, respectively, corresponding to the positions of their axon terminals (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: For most BC types, somata position in INL was correlated with terminal arborization position in IPL.
source: For most types, somata position in INL was correlated with terminal arborization position in IPL (quantified in Figure 5—figure supplement 1P, and summarized in Figure 5L).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1P and Figure 5L.

claim: ACs formed the most heterogeneous class in chicks, with 59 putative types ranging in frequency from 0.4 to 7.2% of all ACs.
source: Similarly, ACs formed the most heterogeneous class in chicks, with 59 putative types (Figures 1G and 6A), ranging in frequency from 0.4 to 7.2% of all ACs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 1G, 6A, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All AC clusters expressed SLC32A1, a transporter that loads both GABA and glycine into synaptic vesicles.
source: All expressed SLC32A1, a transporter that loads both GABA and glycine into synaptic vesicles, and each type expressed either GABAergic markers (GABA transporter, SLC6A1, and the GABA synthetic enzymes, GAD1 and GAD2, 40 clusters) or glycinergic markers (glycine transporter 1, SCL6A9, 19 clusters) (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B.

claim: TFAP2A expression was restricted to ACs in the INL, while TFAP2B was expressed by ACs in both INL and GCL.
source: Expression of two broadly expressed member of the AP2 family of transcription factors, TFAP2A and TFAP2B, distinguished these populations: TFAP2A expression was restricted to ACs in the INL, while TFAP2B was expressed by ACs in both locations (Figure 6B,D,E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B, D, E.

claim: Two AC clusters, AC7 and AC25, expressed cholinergic markers, indicating their identity as starburst amacrine cells (SACs).
source: Two AC clusters, AC7 and AC25, expressed the cholinergic markers choline acetyltransferase (CHAT), choline transporter (SLC5A7), and vesicular acetylcholine transporter (SLC18A3), indicating their identity as SACs.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: AC7 and AC25 are assigned to ON and OFF SACs, respectively.
source: We assign AC7 and AC25 to ON and OFF SACs, respectively, because AC7 expressed FEZF1, a transient marker of developing ON starburst marker in mouse, whereas AC25 expressed TENM3 and ZFHX3, transient OFF markers SAC markers in mouse (Peng et al., 2020; Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citation and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: AC37 is the authentic chick VG3 AC, expressing SLC17A8 (VGlut3) and SDK2.
source: AC37 also expressed the recognition molecule Sidekick 2 (SDK2; Yamagata et al., 2002), which is also a selective marker of mouse VG3 ACs (Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Yamagata and Sanes, 2018), suggesting that AC37 is the authentic chick VG3 AC (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations and Figure 6—figure supplement 2D.

claim: From 8107 single RGC transcriptomes, 41 clusters were resolved ranging in abundance from 0.6 to 5.1% of all RGCs.
source: From 8107 single RGC transcriptomes, we resolved 41 clusters (Figure 7A) ranging in abundance from 0.6 to 5.1% of all RGCs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All RGC clusters expressed the canonical RGC markers RBPMS and THY1, as well as one or more of the Brn3 (POU4F) transcription factors and the RBPMS homolog, RBPMS2.
source: Like RGCs in mammals, all expressed the canonical RGC markers RBPMS and THY1, as well as one or more of the Brn3 (POU4F) transcription factors and the RBPMS homolog, RBPMS2 (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7B.

claim: Cluster 11 selectively expressed OPN4.1 and EOMES, indicating that GC11 is a chick ipRGC type.
source: Among the 41 putative RGC types, cluster 11 selectively expressed OPN4.1, a homolog gene to the defining marker of mammalian intrinsically photosensitive RGCs (ipRGCs), as well as the transcription factor EOMES (Tbr2) (Figure 7B; Figure 7—figure supplement 1I), which is expressed in all but not only ipRGCs (Chaurasia et al., 2005; Mao et al., 2014), indicating that GC11 is a chick ipRGC type.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations and Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1I.

claim: GC25 targets tectal lamina B and GC1 targets tectal lamina F.
source: Based on expression of markers identified in previous studies, we conclude that GC25 targets tectal lamina B (TAC1[substance P]+, NMB [neuromedin B]+, SST [somatostatin I]+, and RELN [reelin]+) and GC1 targets tectal lamina F (CHRNB2 [neuronal acetylcholine receptor beta2 subunit]+, SS2 [somatostatin II], and EZR [ezrin]+) (Yamagata et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citation.

claim: Five Müller glia clusters were distinguished in the single-cell dataset of E18 chick retina.
source: However, we distinguished five clusters in the single-cell dataset of E18 chick retina (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8A and B.

claim: Positional differences underlie Müller glia heterogeneity.
source: This suggested that positional differences might underlie Müller glia heterogeneity.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section as an inference from gene expression patterns.

claim: CHRDL1 (MG1) is selectively expressed in ventral retina, WIF1 (MG2) in dorsal retina, FOXI2 (MG5) in temporal retina, and FOXG1 (BF1) in nasal retina.
source: We documented selective expression of CHRDL1 (MG1) in ventral retina, WIF1 (MG2) in dorsal retina, FOXI2 (MG5) in temporal retina, and FOXG1 (BF1) in nasal retina (Figure 8D–M).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8D-M showing in situ hybridization.

claim: Cells in MG3 cluster were associated with central retina and MG4 with peripheral retina.
source: Finally, in situ hybridization for genes selectively expressed in MG3 (PSCA) and MG4 (TMEM123) indicated that cells in these clusters were associated with central and peripheral retina, respectively (Figure 8N–Q).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8N-Q.

claim: MG3 represents a positionally restricted cell group, whereas MG4 may largely represent immature MGs.
source: Thus, MG3 represents a positionally restricted cell group, whereas MG4 may largely represente immature MGs.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section as a conclusion from developmental analysis.

claim: Reclustering of oligodendrocytes revealed five clusters, all expressing the oligodendrocyte marker OLIG2.
source: Reclustering of oligodendrocytes revealed five clusters (Figure 9A; Figure 9—figure supplement 1A). All expressed the oligodendrocyte marker OLIG2 (Zhou et al., 2001), but they exhibited differential expression of other known markers of developing and mature oligodendrocytes (reviewed in Goldman and Kuypers, 2015), suggesting that they represented different developmental stages.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations and Figure 9A.

claim: Pseudotime analysis arranged the oligodendrocyte clusters in the order: OL5, OL3, OL1, OL2, and OL4.
source: Pseudotime analysis arranged the clusters in the order: OL5, OL3, OL1, OL2, and OL4, and selectively expressed markers supported this order.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: PLP1 and BCAS1 were co-expressed in oligodendrocytes, whereas PDGFRA+ cells formed a distinct population.
source: PLP1 and BCAS1 were co-expressed, whereas PDGFRA+ cells formed a distinct population (Figure 9B; Figure 9—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9B and Figure 9—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: BCAS1+PLP1+ oligodendrocytes were more abundant in central retina than in the periphery, whereas PDGFRA+ cells were more abundant peripherally than centrally.
source: BCAS1+PLP1+ cells were more abundant in central retina, near the optic disc, than in the periphery, whereas PDGFRA+ cells were more abundant peripherally than centrally (Figure 9C–L).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9C-L.

claim: Combining data from chick, mouse, macaque, and human retinal atlases and clustering generated nine clusters, all of which contained cells from all species.
source: To this end, we combined data from the E18/E16 chick atlas with those from our previously published retinal atlases of mouse (Macosko et al., 2015; Shekhar et al., 2016; Tran et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2020a), macaque (Peng et al., 2019), and human (Yan et al., 2020b), and submitted the entire group for clustering. This procedure generated nine clusters, all of which contained cells from all species (Figure 10A,B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section with supporting citations and Figure 10A,B.

claim: Six of the clusters corresponded to major retinal cell classes: rods, cones, HCs, BCs, RGCs, and MG.
source: Six of the clusters corresponded to major retinal cell classes: rods, cones, HCs, BCs, RGCs, and MG.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: The other three clusters were composed of ACs distinguished by neurotransmitter type: GABAergic, glycinergic, and cholinergic+GABAergic (SACs).
source: The other three clusters were composed of ACs distinguished by neurotransmitter type: GABAergic, glycinergic, and cholinergic+GABAergic (SACs); these distinctions are discussed in the next section.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: All retinal cell classes remained transcriptomically similar among species and share expression of key genes used to mark each class in mammals.
source: Despite the >300 million years since the mammalian and avian lineages diverged (Kumar and Hedges, 1998), all classes remained transcriptomically similar among species, and share expression of key genes that have been used to mark each class in mammals (Figure 10).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation and Figure 10.

claim: Types within classes are less well conserved than classes themselves across species.
source: In contrast, types within classes are less well conserved: in only a minority cases, such as PRs, SACs, VG3-ACs and ipRGCs, do chick types have orthologous mammalian types as their closest relatives.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The 136 'mature' cell types in the chick atlas are distributed among seven classes: 8 PRs, 4 HCs, 22 BCs, 59 ACs, 41 RGCs, 1 MG, and 1 oligodendrocyte.
source: The 136 'mature' cell types in our atlas are distributed among seven classes: 8 PRs, 4 HCs, 22 BCs, 59 ACs, 41 RGCs, 1 MG (lumping positional variants, as discussed below), and 1 oligodendrocyte.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The number of cell types in the chick atlas is substantially greater than that deduced from morphological surveys.
source: The number is substantially greater than that deduced from morphological surveys (11 BCs, 26 RGCs; Quesada et al., 1988; Naito and Chen, 2004; reviewed in Seifert et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Microglia, astrocytes or diacytes were not detected in the dataset, even though all are known to be present in chick retina.
source: First, we did not detect microglia, astrocytes or a variant glial type named diacytes (Rompani and Cepko, 2010), even though all are known to be present.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section with supporting citation.

claim: The dataset may have been insufficient to detect the least abundant AC and RGC types.
source: Our sample may have been insufficient to detect still less abundant types: they might have been lumped with related types or missed altogether.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section as a limitation.

claim: The number of AC clusters declined with removal of even 10% of cells, indicating that the dataset was likely too small to capture all types within this class.
source: In contrast, the number of AC clusters declined with removal of even 10% of cells, indicating that our dataset was likely too small to capture all types within this class.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section based on downsampling test results.

claim: The number of cell types in chick is similar to those in mouse, and nearly two-fold higher than those in monkey or human.
source: The number of types in chick is similar to those in mouse, and nearly two-fold higher than those in monkey or human.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section comparing Table 1 data.

claim: The true number of cell types is likely higher in chick than in any mammals sampled to date.
source: Given the sampling limitation discussed above, however, and the larger number of mouse cells profiled (~140,000 vs ~40,000 in chick) we suspect that the true number of types is higher in chick than in any mammals sampled to date.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section as an inference.

claim: An additional 14 clusters represented developmental or positional variants.
source: As noted above, an additional 14 clusters represented developmental or positional variants.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Of 20 eCHIKIN fragments tested, 16 (80%) labeled cells in predicted patterns.
source: Of 20 fragements tested, 16 (80%) labeled cells in predicted patterns, including all cases in which we validated the expression pattern by in situ hybridization or antibodies.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section describing eCHIKIN validation.

claim: To date, only a single Müller glial type has been identified in mice and primates using scRNAseq.
source: To date, only a single Müller glial type has been identified in mice and primates using scRNAseq (Macosko et al., 2015; Shekhar et al., 2016; Peng et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2020b; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Unsupervised analysis of chick Müller glia generated five clusters with a positional basis for the heterogeneity.
source: In contrast, unsupervised analysis of chick Müller glia generated five clusters, which were, however, less well separated from each other than types in other classes. In situ hybridization with probes for genes differentially expressed among these clusters revealed a positional basis for the heterogeneity.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Five of the six Müller glia groups appear to be authentically position-dependent, while the sixth (peripheral) may largely reflect the central-to-peripheral gradient of retinal development.
source: Five of these six groups appear to be authentically position-dependent, based on studies at earlier ages, while the sixth (peripheral) may largely reflect the central-to-peripheral gradient of retinal development that has been observed in several species (Kahn, 1974; Spence and Robson, 1989; Prada et al., 1991; Bruhn and Cepko, 1996).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: 10 clusters fit within cell classes but lacked mature features: four PRs, one HC, one Müller glia, and four oligodendrocytes.
source: Although our aim was to profile mature retinal types, we found 10 clusters that fit within cell classes by our criteria, but lacked mature features: four PRrs, one HC, one Müller glia, and four oligodendrocytes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Several lines of evidence suggested that these 10 clusters were composed of developmental intermediates.
source: Several lines of evidence suggested that these clusters were composed of developmental intermediates.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section.

claim: All retinal cell classes remained transcriptomically similar among chick, mouse, macaque, and human despite >300 million years since mammalian and avian lineages diverged.
source: The answer to first question is clearly yes. Despite the >300 million years since the mammalian and avian lineages diverged (Kumar and Hedges, 1998), all classes remained transcriptomically similar among species, and share expression of key genes that have been used to mark each class in mammals (Figure 10).

claim: In only a minority of cases do chick types have orthologous mammalian types as their closest relatives.
